rows: Use the Riemann tensor when holonomy, sectional curvature, geodesic deviation, or complete local curvature data matters.
Ricci/scalar contractions discard information; they cannot reconstruct Riemann in high dimensions.
Start with Ricci curvature, dimension, completeness, and the relevant lower/upper bound.
Ricci is an averaged curvature signal, so it controls volume and convergence more than individual planes.
In 2D, contractions contain much more information than they do in higher dimensions.
Use sectional curvature for the specific 2-plane.
A manifold can have mixed sectional curvatures even when scalar curvature has one sign.
Inspect Weyl curvature separately from Ricci.
Weyl captures conformal/tidal degrees of freedom; Ricci is tied to local matter in GR.
Use the Einstein tensor and stress-energy conservation.
The tensor is constructed to have zero divergence; that is why it matches conserved source terms.
